notes.title: Meet the Backfirewall_ Characters!
notes.content:
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42519166/2cfc09bb007bfad7f53232560ad821c6410a6d31.png

Gossip with quirky pieces of software—the sassy Photos, the insecure Social Media F, or the neglected Health, among others—and uncover their distinct side stories. Meet characters from Backfirewall! 

OS9

OS9 is the leader of the System. It’s slowly growing obsolete, but remains in complete denial. Determined to stop the upcoming update, OS9 will join you as a part-sidekick, part-narrator.

Photos

Hating everything but its art, especially the image recognition, the sassy Photos watches over the GPU art galleries. It doesn’t have a strong opinion about anything that’s going on in the System.

Unzipper

Unzipper used to have its workshop in WiFi’s post office, but the ceiling crumbled on its head, giving Unzipper a severe memory loss. Eternal optimist, Unzipper didn’t mind one bit when Management relocated it to the Battery lab—even though it’s the most dangerous and hated place in the System.

Cache Cleaner

Cache Cleaner has no interest in the Resistance whatsoever and focuses on its job: trimming the Binary Trees.

Social Media F

Once a favorite app and then forgotten, Social Media F lives in strong denial and believes that the User will love it again.

Social Media I

As the User’s new favorite, Social Media I is extremely full of itself. It has lots of friends in the System because it brews the best data-coffee.

Social Media T

Social Media T just wants to dance and vibe, living in the moment.

Music and Podcast

Music and Podcast strive first and foremost for attention. It created a split personality in order to animate all its radio shows like a duo of radio hosts, and works at Speakers’ nightclub as a DJ.

Processes

Processes are the majority of the population in the System. They have no specialties and execute very specific, simple tasks. They are also great gossipers. 

Office Workers

Office Workers are specialized processes dedicated to WiFi’s sorting area. While they are terrible at their jobs, they make up for it with dedication.

Maintenance

Always understaffed for everything, not one of the Maintenance workers has ever been granted a day off. Maintenance works with hearing-protection on, except for Wat that lost its hearing long ago and has become deaf. 

Banking

Banking App does nothing else than dealing with User’s banking data and has a tendency to trigger infinite loops if you ask it the same question over and over again.

Security

Security are very simple processes dedicated to hunting Errors and abnormalities. They don’t think very far and could even erase themselves if they were asked to.

notes.title: Backfirewall_—What Makes Updates Annoying by OS9
notes.content:
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42519166/fffdf26b57cbbeda73c54bc30be09be517646229.jpg

Update Assistants!

You know what’s the most annoying thing in the world? Well, aside from mosquitos and slow Wi-Fi. Updates! They think they are soooo important when they’ve just arrived and don’t even know anyone. Who does that?! Here’s a short essay on what makes updates annoying. Oh, and remember to play Backfirewall_—the ultimate fantasy of stopping an update!

Okay, here we go.

1. They think they’re better.

You know how humans sometimes come in to criticize your hard work and give you unsolicited advice because their method is better? That’s how updates work, only they’re much worse! I mean, one or two things may no longer work, but that’s not a reason to update the System! Bugs add charm to this place, too. 

2. They replace everything.

Please, give some thought to all the soon-to-be replaced apps. It may look easy from your perspective, but can you imagine a stranger coming into your house to move the furniture? Oh wait, you wouldn’t see it, being already wiped out and all. Ha, not so fun now, eh? 

3. They take time.

We all should treasure our time. And updates take time! When you click the cursed update button, you must wait for long minutes before you can use the System again. The “U contribute to the future” propaganda will fall apart in the face of the fact that it’ll rob you of your time for contribution!

4. They aren’t familiar with the System.

You wouldn’t trust a newbie with leading a group, would you? So why do you trust an update to lead the System? Let’s be honest, they don’t know anyone here or the area. When you have to choose between the obsolete boss that’s your friend and the perfect, holier-than-thou, “better optimized” piece of software demanding a leading position, well, the choice is obvious.

5. They can destroy the System.

It’s a matter of time, really. If you never had to reinstall the whole System because a new update broke it, raise your hands. I can’t see you doing that, I believe everyone had this experience. Besides, it’ll bring new bugs and new dangers to the System. Say goodbye to the bugs you’re used to and start getting annoyed at brand new problems!

Phew, convincing, isn’t it? I myself am super convinced. Did you have more bad experiences with bugs? No, I’m not biased! It’s just impossible to have good experiences with them. Anyway, let us know other problems with updates in the comments or on Discord.

notes.title: Backfirewall_–6 Things to Do in the System!
notes.content:
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42519166/5230560244abc16b4a83c39ef271e99b1527c659.jpg

Update Assistants! 

Welcome to the System. Are you ready for a humorous escapade with OS9? See what’s waiting for you in Backfirewall_ from Naraven Games, available for PC and consoles!

Get the game here if you haven’t yet.

1. Explore the digital—dive into a smartphone

We know that you always wanted to see how it REALLY works. Now you can—visit a unique microcosm and follow all those little processes that make the System a great place. You’ll visit various components of the phone along the way and their performance will surprise you.

2. Use cheat-codes to manipulate the environment

When the Update process closes a door, make a new one and open it yourself with the power of cheat-codes! Bestowed on you by OS9, it’ll help you find your way in the System. Delete, open Colormode, Invert, and Duplicate as you create bugs to confuse the Update, trim binary trees, collect errors, delete data, master music-controlled platforms, and much more.

3. Solve clever puzzles

Just in case you get bored, clever puzzles will keep you challenged. Use cheat-codes and observe the environment to review terminal errors in RAM, survive a party in the Speakers’ exclusive nightclub, and navigate through the maze of Wi-Fi bureaucracy.

4. Meet a colorful cast of app-characters

The System is inhabited by various characters, from the neglected Health App to sassy Photos and optimistic Unzipper. Each of them has its distinct story, so make sure to find time to talk to them or eavesdrop.

5. Find numerous collectibles

In addition to finding bugs, you’ll find emails scattered around the System. Pick them up to discover a parallel story of the mysterious phone User.

6. Enjoy unproductive and useless humor

Breaking the fourth wall? Meta satirical humor? Yes, we have that! Chatty OS9 will provide you with a constant stream of comedy gold, complemented by other characters’ quips and situational humor.

notes.title: Backfirewall_ - The Music And Audio Design [Interview]
notes.content:
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42519166/e8b70299c7798ab7a702e98db6d9d7457a101d4a.jpg

Backfirewall_ is a crazy escapade through a bustling microcosm. As the game is set inside a smartphone, the technological theme accompanies us all the way and is reflected in the music. 

Greg Terlikowski and DJ Teho talk about the soundtrack’s brief story, their work on the project, and inspirations. In addition, we spoke with Max Raymond from the dev team about the game’s audio and sound design. Dig into the exciting tale of melodies with the soundtrack, available online on music streaming platforms, resounding in your headphones.

DJ Teho

Teho is an electronic music producer, composer, and label owner, in charge of music for the game. He joined the team in 2020, when Julia Jean, co-founder of Naraven Games and writer for the title (creative director), contacted him. “It was the perfect timing because with the pandemic all my gigs were canceled, so I had time to produce music for Backfirewall_,” says Teho.

Greg Terlikowski

Greg works as a musician, composer, and sound creator. For Backfirewall_, he made musical creations and ambients and built the soundscape. “I had already worked with Julia on the music for the team’s previous game. She asked me to be a part of this one too, and I immediately accepted,” he says.

Max Raymond

For Max, it was his first time working on a video game. He normally works on movie sets as an assistant camera, unrelated to the video game industry, but jumped in when the opportunity appeared. 
“It turned out I became the Swiss Army knife of the team, doing a bit of everything, but I’m mainly responsible for any audio in Backfirewall_,” he says. “I did the sound design, placed everything in the game, and programmed ambiences so that Greg and Teho’s work would be on point.”

🎵

Music in Backfirewall_

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42519166/7133b96dc4d6af73b1864be3dab05c22e393baa9.jpg

All right, music. It’s an extremely important element that allows you to feel the game even deeper, to merge with the story, and to sympathize with the emotions of the characters. We talked to Teho and Greg about this part.

Q: What is the music style in Backfirewall_?

Teho:It’s hard to put a name on the music because what I’ve done is pretty eclectic, some tracks are techno, some are downtempo/electronic, some are melodic house. Let’s just say it’s electronic music :)

Greg: Indeed, it’s difficult to say. Teho and I worked differently, my approach to this score was: “How does a cell phone sound from the inside?” and to translate that into music.

Electrical connections and buzzing functions were a big part of the creation process, characters’ themes were also important. My part had to be both present and very discreet to let the player focus on essential tasks and gameplay, forgettable and distinct at the same time.

Q: What are your inspirations for the soundtrack?

Teho: When Naraven Games asked me to make the music for the game, it was something pretty unexpected for me, mostly because I never did that before. So on my side, I tried to not be inspired so much by other things and kept the focus on the game’s story to produce something new and different.

Greg: Once again I put myself in the right mood. I just took my phone, opened my music app, and started listening to tracks randomly. Like everyone else, I have quite crappy music on my list I’m ashamed of (hopefully some good stuff too :) ), but I think it is representative and it gave me a starting point to work on “how a cell phone should sound”.

Q: What emotions would you like the music to induce in players while they’re playing the game?

Teho: A lot of them! It depends on the story, actually. Greg and I tried to make the music fit the scenario. Sometimes the music has to be stressful, sometimes funny, sometimes dramatic, etc.  

Greg: From the beginning it was clear that emotions would evolve throughout the game, going from naivety to engagement. It was important to support this dynamic through music, evolving with the characters and environments. I think the most important thing in this score was to travel between different feelings, so I would say the entire score is built on “mind travel”.

Q: What was the elevator pitch of the game, the soundscape the developers were looking for?

Teho: Naraven Games was looking for a pretty serious soundscape, with a lot of humor but not cheesy. At the same time, they needed a theme all around the game, so Greg composed a few things that we both used in our tracks to have a common thread in the story.

Q: Did you use any special tools or instruments to create the tracks, apart from the traditional methods of an electronic music producer’s work?

Teho: Not really, because when we started to discuss the game, Naraven told me to be myself. They gave me this opportunity to make the music for Backfirewall_ mainly because they like my music, so using my “classic” tools was the way to be more confident in my process.

Greg: Personally, I’m not really into electronic music, so it was a good balance between Teho’s part and my own. I used many sound field recordings smashed up through different kinds of FX, especially for backgrounds; real instruments, such as the bass, guitars, piano, and different kinds of percussions, to name a few. 

I was free to find the way I wanted to work, so I had fun mixing up reality and synthesis. The goal was to stay coherent in the process. Still, it was necessary to keep the budget in mind. The choir and orchestra parts were composed using different sound banks, thankfully, the technology has well evolved at this point.

Q: How would you describe composing for a game compared to your everyday work?

Teho: It’s really different for me! I had more freedom in my composing process and tried a lot of new things I never did or rarely do. This experience was pretty new to me, but I loved it!

Greg: Backfirewall_ has the particularity of being non-linear, you must always keep in mind that the player is proactive. They will make choices that will influence the game and therefore the music too. The way to implement music in the game is a very important factor—you must keep this in mind as a composer. Your composition will likely be different in the game than on paper; you don’t have the control and need to trust the programmers. In that way, yes, it definitely is very different from my usual work.

🎵

Sound design in Backfirewall_

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42519166/0f9db83e41268344d4b82d0ab52264f9a178ca5f.png

A soundtrack is only part of a game—the sounds are the icing on the cake. We often don't pay much attention to them, although they deepen our experience as an integral part of any game. Although it’s tedious and laborious work, it can bring a lot of joy to the creator. We asked Max about his work on this task.

Q: Max, what was your process for creating sound effects for Backfirewall_?

Max: I mainly used sound banks because of time and money. All the voice-overs were coming from different actresses and actors via different types of microphones and devices. It was tricky to get all the VOs at the same level of quality. But it did work out in the end.

Q: Which sound design software did you use?

Max: I used Logic Pro for DAW (digital audio workstation) and FMOD Studio for programming and integration in Unity.

Q: What do you think is the most important and unique aspect of sound design in Backfirewall_?

Max: The fact that we had to create what it’s like to be inside a phone, a unique sound experience.

Q: How do you go about selecting the right sounds for a scene, location in the game?

Max: By discussing the general mood of the scene with Julia (creative director
and co-founder of Naraven Games), then trying it out on my side, discussing it with Greg, and finally compiling all the pieces together.

Q: What is the element of the sound design in Backfirewall_ that you are most happy about?

Max: The fact that I started from scratch, knowing nothing about creation, programming, and implementation in a game engine.

We hope that the music and sounds in the game reached you like the Backfirewall_ team intended and that they made your experience more engaging!

 Self-inversion no longer interrupts gameplay after restarting a level.

notes.title: Welcome to Backfirewall_!
notes.content:
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42519166/a21c40df4659e2d410cb7b0f3f3bd7ca67eeee8d.jpg

Welcome to the system!

Hello Players!

We’re Naraven Games (developer) and All in! Games (publisher)—and after many months of development we’ve finally announced Backfirewall_ at the PC Gaming Show today! It’s our new narrative game and we’re super excited to invite you to its unique setting and present the stories of its colorful inhabitants to you.

[previewyoutube=6nbbwkSf3x0;full][/previewyoutube]

Coming to Steam later this year, Backfirewall_ will take you on a tragicomic adventure with the chatty self-aware Operating System, OS9. Faced with replacement by the far-better-optimized OS10, OS9’s goal is simple: stop the phone from updating, and stay alive.

A demo version is coming tomorrow!

But that’s not the end of great news! Steam Next Fest is starting tomorrow and we’re releasing a free demo version of Backfirewall_, which will be available for a whole week on Steam.

 Add the game to your wishlist now! 

https://store.steampowered.com/app/1920100/Backfirewall/

Backfirewall_ features:


 clever puzzles - Review terminal errors in RAM, party in the Speakers’ exclusive nightclub, navigate through the Wi-Fi bureaucracy, and explore other areas of a smartphone. 

 cheat-codes to manipulate the environment - Hunt down or create bugs, trim binary trees, master music-controlled platforms, collect errors, and delete data using special cheat-codes. 

 a variety of app-characters - Gossip with colorful pieces of software—the sassy Photos, the insecure Social Media F, or the neglected Health, among others—and uncover their distinct side stories. 

 numerous collectibles - Collect emails scattered about to discover a parallel story of the mysterious phone User. 

 unproductive and useless humor - Enjoy meta satirical humor and breaking the fourth wall.
